podcast.body: Featured on their self-titled debut album from 1992, this track exemplifies the powerful sound achieved through producer Garth Richardson's unique recording method. The album was recorded with the band playing through a concert PA system, and the speakers were mic'd to capture a live feel, making it an outstanding listen on high-fidelity systems like "180 gram vinyl" or a big stereo. "Still, one of the greatest debut records of all time, Rage Against the Machine from 1992."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song is the opening track of Rage Against The Machine's 1992 debut record. The instrumental intro for "Bombtrack" was a piece Tom Morello had leftover from his previous band, Lock Up. The main riff of the song was derived from "Alice in My Fantacies" by Funkadelic, a track from their 1974 album "Standing on the Verge of Getting It On." "Bomb track, the first song, and they're amazing, 1992 first record."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
